moduleTitle: Enhancing test workflows with integrations in Tricentis Testim
learningObjectives: Explain how to integrate tests with CI using Testim CLI and how to connect it to major CIs using a simple shell command.
Summarize the steps to set up and integrate Testim with Azure DevOps.
Discuss the process of linking a test in Testim to a test case in TTM for Jira and interpreting test results.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: CI integration recap: the CLI is the universal connector

elements.description: The npm CLI can run from a suitably configured CI runner. Supported runtime, project/grid, credentials and network access are prerequisites; a shell command alone does not provision or validate an integration.

elements.text: This is the same underlying mechanism covered for Jenkins earlier in this path — Azure DevOps integration (next section) uses the identical CLI, just wired into Azure Pipelines' own YAML syntax instead of a Jenkinsfile/build step.

bulletPoints: Same CLI, same install command, across every major CI platform.
No platform-specific plugin required — just a shell command any CI runner can execute.

elements.description: The Azure guide demonstrates runtime/CLI setup, execution and PublishTestResults JUnit collection. Its Node 10.x example is obsolete; validate supported runtime and secure credentials instead of treating the snippet as production-ready.

elements.text: This cited workflow invokes tests and publishes JUnit results. It does not by itself map Azure work items; that is a scope statement about this workflow, not proof every possible Azure integration is unsupported.

bulletPoints: Azure DevOps setup = a YAML code snippet (install Node.js + Testim CLI, then run the CLI) added to the pipeline.
JUnit publication is distinct from automatically mapping Azure work items.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Linking a test to TTM for Jira and viewing results

elements.description: Settings > Integrations > Test Management contains separate TTM and Xray modules. TTM setup uses a TTM API key and project selection; Xray requires its documented Jira/Xray credentials. Connecting a project does not map its individual tests.

elements.term: Linking a test to a TTM for Jira test case
elements.description: Map a Testim test from Setup properties to one or multiple TTM test cases. Bulk create-and-map skips tests already mapped and reports failures for retry. Only one TMS connection is supported at a time; disconnecting removes mappings.

elements.term: Viewing results in TTM for Jira
elements.description: Mapped Remote Grid runs report names and translated statuses to TTM execution results. Mandatory custom fields are unsupported. Mapping and authentication must remain valid; generating a run does not guarantee delivery.

elements.text: Remote Grid reporting eligibility is separate from subscription quota: some local CLI/library runs count toward quota without qualifying for this TTM remote-reporting workflow.

bulletPoints: Use the TTM API key and select projects, then map tests separately.
Multiple mapped cases are supported; bulk mapping skips existing mappings.
Remote Grid reporting and quota are distinct; inspect translated statuses and connection requirements.

examPitfalls.title: Expecting Azure DevOps integration to link test cases to work items like TTM for Jira does
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Assuming the Azure DevOps integration automatically updates test results and links test cases to Azure DevOps work items, the way TTM for Jira links to Jira test cases.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: The cited Azure YAML invokes tests and publishes JUnit, but does not itself configure work-item mapping. Avoid treating that scope as a universal prohibition.

examPitfalls.title: Running a mapped test from the local editor and expecting it in TTM for Jira
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Running a test linked to a TTM for Jira test case from the Testim Visual Editor, then checking TTM for Jira's Test Execution tab and finding nothing.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Use the documented mapped Remote Grid workflow and verify reporting. Quota-counted local execution is not the same as remote reporting eligibility.

practiceQuiz.scenario: The cited Azure YAML alone automatically maps Testim cases to Azure work items, without separately configured mapping.
practiceQuiz.hint: Publishing a JUnit report is distinct from work-item mapping.
practiceQuiz.rationale: False: the cited YAML runs the CLI and publishes JUnit results; it does not configure work-item mapping by itself. This does not prove every custom mapping workflow is unsupported.

optionExplanations.A: The snippet publishes JUnit but does not configure that mapping.
optionExplanations.B: False: separate mapping setup would be required.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which settings section contains the separate TTM for Jira and Xray integration modules?
practiceQuiz.hint: The top-level settings tab is 'Integration' — Test Management is a section inside it.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Settings > Integrations contains Test Management modules. TTM API-key setup and Xray Jira/client credentials are different; selecting the section is not the complete connection setup.

optionExplanations.A: Test Plans is not the cited integration section.
optionExplanations.B: This reverses the documented integration-section hierarchy.
optionExplanations.C: Reports is not the documented module section.
optionExplanations.D: The Test Management section is under Integrations settings.

practiceQuiz.scenario: With a supported runtime and configured access, the npm Testim CLI can be invoked by a CI runner that supports the required command.
practiceQuiz.hint: This is the core reason the CLI works the same way across Jenkins, Azure DevOps, GitHub Actions, etc.
practiceQuiz.rationale: True: configured CI runners can invoke the CLI. Dependency installation, access and result collection remain required.

optionExplanations.A: The configured npm CLI can be invoked by the stated runner.
optionExplanations.B: The documented CI guides support such invocation.

quickRecap.value: Same npm-installed CLI works across every major CI that can run a shell command.
Configured Azure runner executes CLI and publishes JUnit; mapping is a separate setup.
Integrations > Test Management → TTM for Jira / Xray modules.
One Testim test can map to multiple TTM cases; bulk workflow skips existing mappings.

quickRecap.key: Viewing results in TTM for Jira
quickRecap.value: Mapped Remote Grid reporting eligibility is distinct from quota counting; verify integration delivery.
